instructions:
# API Versioning

## What this skill does
Design versioning for APIs. Covers the four main schemes - URI path, query string, custom header, and media type negotiation - plus deprecation signaling with Deprecation and Sunset headers.

## When to use
- Adding breaking changes to an existing API
- Migrating consumers to a new endpoint shape
- Choosing a scheme for a greenfield API

## Real commands
```bash
# URI path versioning
curl -s https://api.example.com/v2/users

# Custom header versioning
curl -s -H 'X-Api-Version: 2024-01-15' https://api.example.com/users

# Media type (content negotiation) versioning
curl -s -H 'Accept: application/vnd.example.v2+json' https://api.example.com/users
curl -s -H 'Accept: application/vnd.example+json;version=2' https://api.example.com/users

# Query string versioning
curl -s 'https://api.example.com/users?api-version=2'

# Verify deprecation signaling
curl -sI https://api.example.com/v1/users | grep -iE 'deprecation|sunset'

# Compare versions side by side
diff <(curl -s https://api.example.com/v1/users | jq -S .) <(curl -s https://api.example.com/v2/users | jq -S .)
```

## Header conventions
```http
Deprecation: true
Sunset: Fri, 31 Jan 2025 23:59:59 GMT
```

## Best practices
- Never remove a version without a published Sunset date
- Keep at least 6 months between deprecation and sunset
- Route versions at the gateway, not inside controllers
- Document the versioning policy in the API reference

## Testing
```bash
curl -s https://api.example.com/v1/users -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
curl -s -H 'X-Api-Version: 9999-01-01' https://api.example.com/users -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
```

examples.input: Add v2 while keeping v1 alive
examples.output: Adds the v2 routes behind the gateway, verifies both respond, and sets a Sunset header on v1.
Checks the Deprecation and Sunset headers on v1 and reports the retirement date.
